# Weekly close-location / participation state model - development report

**Strategy:** `family-ml-microstructure` / frozen primary `ridge5_ms_clv5_vol5_f25`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 -> 2023-12-29 (development only; 2024-2026 never loaded)
**Marks:** 1-minute, next-open fills, 2% band
**Bar:** TQQQ dev 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe

## Verdict

**Pass on the development window at 1, 5 and 10 bp, with a 45.9-46.1% max
drawdown.** The frozen cell is a walk-forward ridge model on two
session-shape features - 5-day close location and 5-day volume participation -
that predicts the next 5-session TQQQ return and holds TQQQ when the forecast
is above a quarter of the training mean, sized to a 45% volatility budget.

The honest qualification is that **the ML is not clearly additive over a
simple rule.** A fixed weekly `clv5<=0.25` gate gets 44.11% / 40.20% / 1.16 at
1 bp, and a fixed daily `volr<=0.25` gate gets 51.19% / 37.05% / 1.34. The ML
primary has a higher CAGR than the weekly rule but a higher drawdown; the
simple daily participation rule beats it on all three headline statistics at
1 bp. The family's edge is fast close-location / participation timing, not a
new ML alpha. The pass is real but it is a risk-managed TQQQ beta, not
independent alpha.

## Frozen-cell confirmation

The pre-freeze scratch log reported **51.67% CAGR / 45.93% DD / 1.20 Sharpe /
70.8% average TQQQ weight / 849 fills** for this cell. That number is
reproduced exactly when the refit calendar is stopped at 2023-10-01, which
leaves November-December 2023 at the 1.0 warm-up weight:

| run | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | avg TQQQ | fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| pre-freeze calendar (`refit_end=2023-10-01`) | 51.67% | 45.93% | 1.20 | 70.8% | 849 |
| clean full calendar (all of 2023 predicted) | **49.81%** | **45.93%** | **1.18** | **70.2%** | **859** |

The 1.86 pp difference is entirely the two months the old scratch left on the
warm-up weight; the model, features, hurdle, refit frequency and execution are
unchanged. The clean, holdout-ready run is the headline below. Both versions
pass the bar at 1/5/10 bp.

## 1. Headline

### Development window, 1-minute marks

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Avg TQQQ wt | Fills | Turnover |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **1 bp** | **49.81%** | **45.93%** | **1.18** | 1.65 | 42.0% | 70.2% | 859 | 1,594x |
| 5 bp | 48.46% | 46.00% | 1.16 | 1.62 | 42.0% | 70.2% | 859 | 1,594x |
| 10 bp | 46.79% | 46.07% | 1.13 | 1.59 | 42.0% | 70.2% | 859 | 1,594x |

$100k at 1 bp ends at **$2,521,565** over 7.98 years. The 1 bp headline beats
the 36.72% bar by **13.1 pp** with a drawdown **36.4 pp below** the 82.29%
bar and 14.1 pp below the 60% target.

### Benchmarks, same window and marks

| Asset / control | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TQQQ buy-and-hold | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 |
| TQQQ official bar | 36.72% | 82.29% | 0.82 |
| QQQ buy-and-hold | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.90 |
| BIL | 1.39% | 0.24% | 0.92 |
| Vol-target only (45%, same sizing) | 38.77% | 59.97% | 0.97 |
| **Frozen ML primary (1 bp)** | **49.81%** | **45.93%** | **1.18** |

The volatility-target-only control already clears the CAGR bar, so the ML
signal must be judged on what it adds on top of it: **+11.0 pp CAGR and
-14.0 pp drawdown**, at a similar vol budget. That is the real contribution;
it is not a claim that the raw signal beats TQQQ without sizing.

## 2. What the strategy does

### Features (session shape, intraday only)

For each session `d`, using adjusted 1-minute bars and the **15:58** signal
bar (the second-to-last regular bar):

```
CLV_d  = 2*(C_d - L_d)/(H_d - L_d) - 1     # close location in the day's range
VOLR_d = log(V_d / mean(V_{d-20..d-1}))    # participation vs its own trailing mean
clv5_d  = mean(CLV_{d-4..d})
volr5_d = mean(VOLR_{d-4..d})
```

The signal bar is strictly before the 15:59 fill. The high, low, close and
volume all use data through 15:58; the 15:59 bar is only the execution price.

### Label and model

```
y5_d = entry(d+5) / entry(d) - 1           # next 5-session holding return
model = ridge, L2=30, expanding window, monthly refit
train = every 5th session (block starts), labels realised >= 9 days before test
scale = training mean/std only, clip +/-5
hurdle = 0.25 * training mean of y5
```

### Allocation and execution

```
sigma20 = annualised stdev of last 20 entry-to-entry TQQQ returns through d-1
base_vt = clip(0.45 / sigma20, 0, 1)
w       = base_vt * 1{predicted y5 >= 0.25 * training_mean}
remainder = BIL
decision  = every 5 sessions, at the 15:58 signal bar
fill      = next bar open (15:59)
hold      = 5 sessions
```

The 5-session horizon is deliberate. A daily gate on the same signal turned
over too much to survive 5-10 bp costs; the weekly state is persistent and
cost-robust. It is still a short-horizon microstructure state, not a slow
trend or volatility regime.

### Warm-up disclosure

The first model prediction is **2017-04-04**; the minimum training window is
60 five-session blocks. From 2016-01-04 to 2017-04-03 the strategy holds the
1.0 warm-up weight (100% TQQQ). The 2016 return is therefore exactly TQQQ's
+18.6%. This is disclosed and is not part of the claimed edge. On the
model-only period (2017-04-04 -> 2023-12-29) the strategy still makes
**49.68% CAGR / 44.51% max DD**, versus TQQQ **33.64% / 81.68%**. The pass is
not a warm-up artifact.

## 3. Pre-registered grid and plateau

The grid was fixed around the frozen cell before the final run. The primary
was not changed after seeing the results.

| # | id | features | refit | hurdle | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | avg TQQQ | pass 1 bp |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | **clv5_vol5_m_f25 (frozen)** | clv5, volr5 | monthly | 0.25 | **49.81%** | **45.93%** | **1.18** | 70.2% | yes |
| 2 | clv5_vol5_m_f50 | clv5, volr5 | monthly | 0.50 | 41.01% | 45.93% | 1.05 | 64.5% | yes |
| 3 | clv5_vol5_m_f75 | clv5, volr5 | monthly | 0.75 | 34.29% | 45.93% | 0.96 | 58.0% | no |
| 4 | clv5_vol5_q_f25 | clv5, volr5 | quarterly | 0.25 | 49.36% | 45.93% | 1.18 | 69.9% | yes |
| 5 | clv5_m_f25 | clv5 | monthly | 0.25 | 38.63% | 60.56% | 0.97 | 77.1% | yes |
| 6 | clv5_m_f50 | clv5 | monthly | 0.50 | 41.34% | 55.96% | 1.03 | 70.5% | yes |
| 7 | volr5_m_f25 | volr5 | monthly | 0.25 | 40.57% | 62.82% | 1.00 | 77.0% | yes |
| 8 | clv5_vol5_last5_m_f25 | clv5, volr5, last30_5 | monthly | 0.25 | 36.64% | 45.50% | 0.99 | 64.8% | no |

**6 of 8 cells pass the formal bar at 1 bp.** The plateau is broad in the
feature direction: the two-feature cell, the quarterly cell, both one-feature
cells and the 50% hurdle all clear 36.72%. It is not flat in the hurdle
direction: 0.75 is too conservative and falls to 34.29%. The 3-feature cell
misses by 0.08 pp (36.64%), i.e. it is at the bar, not safely above it.

The primary is the highest-CAGR cell. That is a consequence of the freeze,
not a post-hoc promotion: the cell was fixed from the cost-robust weekly
screen before this run, and no other cell was substituted after the results.

## 4. Feature ablation

| Feature set | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | avg TQQQ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| clv5 + volr5 (primary) | 49.81% | 45.93% | 1.18 | 70.2% |
| clv5 only | 38.63% | 60.56% | 0.97 | 77.1% |
| volr5 only | 40.57% | 62.82% | 1.00 | 77.0% |
| last30_5 only | 32.96% | 49.66% | 0.90 | - |
| gap5 + first30_5 + mid5 | 25.61% | 66.07% | 0.75 | - |
| full shape (adds day5, rng5) | 30.73% | 49.31% | 0.89 | - |

Both single features clear the formal CAGR bar but with drawdowns above the
60% target. The combination is the only configuration that clears both the
CAGR bar and the 60% DD target, which is consistent with the mechanism:
close location says *which way* the week is likely to revert; participation
says *whether the session was significant*. Adding the other session-shape
features (gap, first 30m, midday, range) **hurts**: the model overfits noise
and the full-shape cell falls to 30.73%. This is a useful negative result and
the reason the grid is deliberately small.

## 5. Placebo

All placebos use the same model, hurdle, sizing and 1 bp cost. Labels or
training features are permuted within each monthly training window; the
timing placebo shifts the features by one 5-session block.

| Placebo | mean CAGR | p5 | p50 | p95 | real | real percentile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| shuffled training labels (20) | 35.48% | 26.75% | 35.01% | 45.31% | 49.81% | 100% |
| shuffled training features (20) | 36.15% | 26.94% | 36.03% | 44.52% | 49.81% | 95% |
| features shifted 5 sessions (1) | 36.37% | - | - | - | 49.81% | - |

The real strategy is above all 20 label placebos and 19 of 20 feature
placebos, and shifting the features one block destroys the edge (36.37% CAGR,
60.08% DD, 0.95 Sharpe). But the separation is modest: the placebos are
structurally high because they inherit the long TQQQ / 45% vol-target
exposure, which alone makes 38.77%. The ML's incremental edge over the
placebo mean is about 14 pp; over the 95th percentile it is about 5 pp. This
is evidence that the timing is not random, but not overwhelming evidence of a
large, stable signal.

## 6. Cut tests and causality

Two pre-cut rebuilds were run on data truncated at a block-aligned date:

| Cut | Sessions compared | Max abs weight difference | Changed > 1e-12 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2020-06-30 | 1,130 | 0.0 | 0 |
| 2022-06-30 | 1,635 | 0.0 | 0 |

The pre-cut weights are bit-identical. Every feature is a trailing statistic
through the 15:58 signal bar; the label uses only past 5-session blocks; the
model standardisation uses training rows only; the volatility target uses
returns through the prior session; and the walk-forward refits only on labels
realised at least 9 calendar days before the test month. There is no
full-sample scaling and no holdout loading.

## 7. Yearly, subperiods and drawdown

### Yearly returns

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ | Difference |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | 18.6% | 18.6% | 0.0 pp (warm-up) |
| 2017 | 131.6% | 113.0% | +18.6 pp |
| 2018 | 8.7% | -23.5% | +32.2 pp |
| 2019 | 61.7% | 130.5% | -68.8 pp |
| 2020 | 43.7% | 99.8% | -56.1 pp |
| 2021 | 103.1% | 90.9% | +12.2 pp |
| 2022 | -31.4% | -79.7% | +48.3 pp |
| 2023 | 134.8% | 204.9% | -70.1 pp |

The pattern is the familiar one: the strategy gives up a lot of upside in
strong bull years (2019, 2020, 2023) and earns its compounding edge by losing
much less in 2018 and 2022. It is not a broad all-weather alpha. The 2021 and
2017 beats are real but smaller than the bull-year give-ups.

### Subperiods

| Period | Strategy CAGR | max DD | TQQQ CAGR | TQQQ max DD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 51.45% | 34.32% | 48.60% | 57.97% |
| 2020-2021 | 67.45% | 44.51% | 91.47% | 69.89% |
| 2022-2023 | 26.33% | 34.16% | -22.33% | 81.05% |

The strongest relative contribution is 2022-2023: +48.7 pp of CAGR and 47 pp
less drawdown. The 2020-2021 period lags TQQQ badly on CAGR, which is the
cost of the participation filter during the post-COVID melt-up.

### Drawdown

The maximum drawdown is **45.93%** on 1-minute marks; on the daily equity
series the drawdown window is **2020-02-19 to 2020-03-12 at 44.51%** - the
COVID crash, not 2022. The strategy did not avoid the initial COVID gap; it
avoided the 2022 grind (-31.4% vs -79.7%). The drawdown improvement over TQQQ
is therefore mostly a 2022 story, not a 2020 one.

## 8. Exposure, correlation and what this is

- Average TQQQ weight: **70.2%**; fully invested 42.3% of sessions, zero
  TQQQ 13.7%; 211 weekly weight changes; 859 fills over 8 years.
- Daily correlation to TQQQ: **0.861**; to QQQ: **0.858**.
- The remainder is BIL. The strategy is long-only, weights >= 0, row sums
  <= 1.

This is a high-beta TQQQ timing overlay. It is not market-neutral, not
diversifying, and not a hedge. Its value is a better compounding path than
TQQQ buy-and-hold, paid for by giving up upside in strong bull years.

## 9. Simple-rule comparison: does the ML add anything?

| Rule | Cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Frozen ML primary** | 1 bp | **49.81%** | **45.93%** | **1.18** |
| | 5 bp | 48.46% | 46.00% | 1.16 |
| | 10 bp | 46.79% | 46.07% | 1.13 |
| Weekly `clv5<=0.25` x VT | 1 bp | 44.11% | 40.20% | 1.16 |
| | 5 bp | 41.90% | 40.20% | 1.12 |
| | 10 bp | 39.18% | 40.20% | 1.07 |
| Daily `volr<=0.25` x VT | 1 bp | 51.19% | 37.05% | 1.34 |
| | 5 bp | 46.12% | 38.08% | 1.24 |
| | 10 bp | 39.98% | 39.68% | 1.12 |
| Vol-target only | 1 bp | 38.77% | 59.97% | 0.97 |
| TQQQ buy-and-hold | 1 bp | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 |

The ML primary is **not clearly additive**:

- Against the fixed weekly close-location rule it adds +5.7 pp CAGR at 1 bp,
  but also +5.7 pp drawdown; the Sharpe is essentially identical (1.18 vs
  1.16). At 10 bp the ML is +7.6 pp CAGR and +0.06 Sharpe, so the extra
  feature and continuous forecast do buy something at higher costs.
- Against the fixed **daily** participation rule, the ML loses at 1 bp on
  every metric (49.81/45.93/1.18 vs 51.19/37.05/1.34). At 5 bp the ML has a
  higher CAGR (48.46 vs 46.12) but a higher drawdown and lower Sharpe. At
  10 bp the two Sharpe ratios are effectively tied (1.13 vs 1.12).

The honest reading is that the edge is a **fast close-location /
participation filter**, and the ML is a convenient but not superior way to
implement it. The 5-day horizon and the volume feature are what make the ML
cell cost-robust, but a simple daily volume gate is already cost-robust at
10 bp and has a better drawdown. The ML should not be presented as a new
source of alpha.

## 10. Family purity

- The primary predictors are **intraday session-shape price/volume
  features**: 5-day mean close location (CLV) and 5-day mean volume
  participation (VOLR). Both are built from 1-minute bars through 15:58.
- No daily realised volatility, drawdown, trend SMA or relative-strength
  feature is used as a predictor. The 45% volatility target is **risk
  control only**; it is not in the signal.
- `rng` (intraday range) was deliberately excluded from the primary and the
  grid. An exploratory screen showed that a range filter is a volatility
  proxy and carries most of the daily-gate result, which would violate the
  family mandate. The grid's full-shape ablation includes `rng5` and is
  worse (30.73%), so the frozen model does not depend on it.
- Caveat: `volr5` is correlated with the session range (about 0.48), so the
  participation leg is partly a fast volatility/participation proxy. The
  one-feature ablations show that neither leg alone clears both the CAGR bar
  and the 60% DD target; the combination is what works. This is disclosed
  rather than presented as pure directional alpha.

## 11. Honest verdict

What is supported:

- The frozen weekly ML cell clears the stated development bar at **1, 5 and
  10 bp**: 49.81% / 48.46% / 46.79% CAGR, 45.9-46.1% max DD, 1.18 / 1.16 /
  1.13 Sharpe. The pre-freeze 51.67% / 45.93% / 1.20 is reproduced exactly
  under its original calendar; the clean full-calendar run is 49.81%.
- The pass is not a warm-up artifact: the model-only period is 49.68% /
  44.51% versus TQQQ 33.64% / 81.68%.
- The pre-cut weights are bit-identical at two cut dates. There is no
  full-sample scaling or holdout loading.
- The signal is above all label-shuffle placebos and 19/20 feature-shuffle
  placebos, and shifting the features one block destroys the edge.
- The grid shows a broad feature plateau: 6/8 cells clear the bar, including
  both one-feature variants and the quarterly refit.

What is not supported:

- The ML is **not additive** over a simple rule. The fixed daily
  `volr<=0.25` gate is better on CAGR, drawdown and Sharpe at 1 bp, and has a
  comparable 10 bp profile. The weekly ML's advantage is mainly against the
  weekly close-location rule, not against the best simple participation rule.
- The edge is concentrated in crash avoidance: 2018 +32 pp and 2022 +48 pp
  versus TQQQ, with large give-ups in 2019, 2020 and 2023. The 2020-2021
  subperiod lags TQQQ by 24 pp of CAGR.
- The maximum drawdown is the 2020 COVID crash (45.93%), not a 2022
  drawdown. The strategy is not a crash hedge.
- The placebo separation over the 95th percentile is only about 5 pp. The
  placebos are structurally high because they inherit the vol-targeted TQQQ
  exposure.
- The 3-feature cell and the high-hurdle cell fail; the plateau is not flat
  in every direction.

Bottom line: this is a **verified, cost-robust TQQQ risk-management overlay**
that clears the development bar with a 46% drawdown, but it is not independent
alpha and the ML is not clearly better than a simple participation rule. It
should be presented as a close-location / participation timing strategy, not
as an ML discovery.

## 12. Reproduction

```powershell
cd C:\Users\27175\Desktop\quant-trader-research
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\Users\27175\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\pylibs"
$env:BT_THREADS = "1"

```

`strategy.py` builds the session features from adjusted 1-minute bars,
runs the 8-cell walk-forward grid, the 1/5/10 bp cost ladder, the placebo
and cut tests, and writes `result.json`. The public entry point is
`build_weights(ts, o, c)`: it accepts the daily panel and uses only data up to
`ts[-1]`, with `features` supplied or rebuilt from 1-minute bars. The refit
loop runs to the last month in `ts`, so extending the window extends the
walk-forward without retuning.

## 13. Files

- `HYPOTHESIS.md` - pre-registration and frozen grid.
- `strategy.py` - causal implementation, grid, placebo, cut tests.
- `result.json` - full numbers.
- `report.md` - this file.

# Weekly close-location / participation state model - pre-registration

**Status:** primary frozen before the final 8-cell 1-minute run.
**Window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 only. Nothing on or after
2024-01-01 is loaded or inspected by `strategy.py`.
**Family:** statistical / ML microstructure, weekly state.

## Frozen primary

```
id            ridge5_ms_clv5_vol5_f25
features      clv5, volr5
label         y5 = entry(d+5) / entry(d) - 1
model         ridge, L2 = 30, expanding training, monthly refit
hurdle        0.25 * training_mean(y5)
sizing        base_vt = clip(0.45 / sigma20, 0, 1), sigma20 from entry
              returns through session d-1 (shifted one day)
decision      every 5 sessions, at the 15:58 signal bar
fill          next bar open (15:59)
hold          5 sessions
```

The primary is frozen from the cost-robust weekly screen. It is not a
post-hoc promotion: the grid below is centred on this cell, and no other cell
will be promoted after the final run.

## Hypothesis

The shape of the trading session carries information about the next few
sessions that survives the next open:

- **Close location (CLV)** = where the session closed inside its own range,
  `2*(C-L)/(H-L) - 1`, bounded in [-1, +1]. A close near the high is late
  buying / short covering; a close near the low is capitulation. At a
  one-to-five-session horizon TQQQ mean-reverts against the close location:
  weak closes are followed by better returns than strong closes.
- **Participation (volume ratio)** = log(volume / trailing 20-session mean
  volume). High participation confirms that the session's close location was
  an event, not noise. The model may learn an interaction; the frozen cell is
  linear in the two features.

A walk-forward ridge model estimates the next **5-session** TQQQ return from
5-day trailing means of these session-shape features. The 5-session horizon is
deliberate: a daily gate on the same signal turns over too much to survive
5-10 bp costs, while the weekly state is persistent and cost-robust. It is
still a short-horizon microstructure state, not a slow trend, volatility or
relative-strength regime.

The position is TQQQ when the predicted 5-session return is at least
`0.25 * training_mean`, scaled by a 45% volatility budget; the remainder is
BIL. The volatility target is risk control only.

## Rules (exact)

Data: adjusted 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL bars, regular session.

```
For session d:
  signal bar   = second-to-last 1-minute bar (15:58 on a normal day)
  entry bar    = last 1-minute bar (15:59)
  O,H,L,C,V    = session open, and high/low/close/volume through the signal bar
  CLV_d        = 2*(C-L)/(H-L) - 1
  VOLR_d       = log(V / mean(V_{d-20..d-1}))
  clv5_d       = mean(CLV_{d-4..d})            # 5-day trailing mean
  volr5_d      = mean(VOLR_{d-4..d})
  y5_d         = entry_{d+5} / entry_d - 1     # next 5-session return

Model (walk-forward, monthly refit):
  features     = [clv5, volr5]
  training set = block starts every 5 sessions, expanding window,
                 labels realised at least 9 calendar days before the test month
  standardise  = training mean/std only, clip +/-5
  estimator    = ridge, L2 = 30, target standardised by training mean/std

Allocation (set at the 15:58 close of a block start, filled at the 15:59 open):
  sigma20      = annualised stdev of the last 20 entry-to-entry TQQQ returns
                 through session d-1 (shifted one day, causal)
  base_vt      = clip(0.45 / sigma20, 0, 1)
  w            = base_vt * 1{predicted y5 >= 0.25 * training_mean}
  remainder    = BIL
  hold         = 5 sessions, rebalance at the next block start
```

Before the first model prediction (2016-07-01), the default weight is 1.0
TQQQ. This warm-up is disclosed and is not part of the claimed edge.

Fills are next-open: the weight at bar 15:58 is executed at the open of bar
15:59. The 2% no-trade band and all slippage are handled by `research/bt.py`.

## Pre-registered grid (8 cells)

All cells use L2 = 30, expanding training, 5-session blocks, the same 45%
volatility budget, and the same `pred >= hurdle * training_mean` allocation.
The primary is cell 1; the grid is centred on it. No cell will be promoted
after the final run.

| # | id | features | refit | hurdle |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | `clv5_vol5_m_f25` **FROZEN PRIMARY** | clv5, volr5 | monthly | 0.25 |
| 2 | `clv5_vol5_m_f50` | clv5, volr5 | monthly | 0.50 |
| 3 | `clv5_vol5_m_f75` | clv5, volr5 | monthly | 0.75 |
| 4 | `clv5_vol5_q_f25` | clv5, volr5 | quarterly | 0.25 |
| 5 | `clv5_m_f25` | clv5 | monthly | 0.25 |
| 6 | `clv5_m_f50` | clv5 | monthly | 0.50 |
| 7 | `volr5_m_f25` | volr5 | monthly | 0.25 |
| 8 | `clv5_vol5_last5_m_f25` | clv5, volr5, last30_5 | monthly | 0.25 |

The grid isolates the feature contribution (cells 5-7), the hurdle (1-3), the
refit frequency (4), and a third feature (8).

## Pass criteria

- Dev CAGR > 36.72% and max DD < 82.29% at 1 bp.
- Target: max DD < 60%.
- Report 1/5/10 bp for the primary. A cell that only passes at 1 bp is a fail
  for the programme's purposes.
- Report the whole grid, not just the best cell.

## Falsifiers

- The label-shuffle or feature-shuffle placebo matches the real CAGR/DD.
- Shifting the features by one block (5 sessions) leaves the result intact.
- The cut test changes pre-cut weights.
- The edge is one year (2022) or one crash episode.
- A simple fixed rule on `clv5` matches the ML.
- The 5 bp or 10 bp CAGR falls below 36.72%.
- Removing `volr5` (cell 5) or `clv5` (cell 7) leaves the result unchanged, in
  which case the two-feature claim is not supported.

## What this is not

- Not a trend, volatility-regime, relative-strength or drawdown-recovery
  strategy. The primary predictors are session close location and volume
  participation, both from intraday 1-minute bars. `rng` (intraday range) is
  deliberately excluded from the primary and the grid: an exploratory screen
  showed a range filter is a volatility proxy and carries most of the daily
  gate result, which would violate the family mandate. The 45% vol target is
  risk control only.
- Not market-neutral: correlation to TQQQ will be high.
- Not a claim that the ML is additive over a simple close-location or volume
  threshold; the report tests that directly.

## Exploratory disclosure

Before freezing this cell, the following were examined on the development
window and are reported in `report.md`: (i) next-session open-to-open
classifiers/regressions on the full session-shape feature set; (ii) depth-1/2
CART trees with and without `rng`; (iii) daily close-location and volume
gates with hysteresis; (iv) a 1-session-label weekly variant; (v) the weekly
ridge feature/hurdle/refit surface. None of those is part of the pass
evidence. The frozen cell was chosen because the daily gate was cost-fragile
and the weekly two-feature state was cost-robust, not because it maximised a
single dev statistic.

## 2. What the strategy does

### Features (session shape, intraday only)

For each session `d`, using adjusted 1-minute bars and the **15:58** signal
bar (the second-to-last regular bar):

```
CLV_d  = 2*(C_d - L_d)/(H_d - L_d) - 1     # close location in the day's range
VOLR_d = log(V_d / mean(V_{d-20..d-1}))    # participation vs its own trailing mean
clv5_d  = mean(CLV_{d-4..d})
volr5_d = mean(VOLR_{d-4..d})
```

The signal bar is strictly before the 15:59 fill. The high, low, close and
volume all use data through 15:58; the 15:59 bar is only the execution price.

### Label and model

```
y5_d = entry(d+5) / entry(d) - 1           # next 5-session holding return
model = ridge, L2=30, expanding window, monthly refit
train = every 5th session (block starts), labels realised >= 9 days before test
scale = training mean/std only, clip +/-5
hurdle = 0.25 * training mean of y5
```

### Allocation and execution

```
sigma20 = annualised stdev of last 20 entry-to-entry TQQQ returns through d-1
base_vt = clip(0.45 / sigma20, 0, 1)
w       = base_vt * 1{predicted y5 >= 0.25 * training_mean}
remainder = BIL
decision  = every 5 sessions, at the 15:58 signal bar
fill      = next bar open (15:59)
hold      = 5 sessions
```

The 5-session horizon is deliberate. A daily gate on the same signal turned
over too much to survive 5-10 bp costs; the weekly state is persistent and
cost-robust. It is still a short-horizon microstructure state, not a slow
trend or volatility regime.

### Warm-up disclosure

The first model prediction is **2017-04-04**; the minimum training window is
60 five-session blocks. From 2016-01-04 to 2017-04-03 the strategy holds the
1.0 warm-up weight (100% TQQQ). The 2016 return is therefore exactly TQQQ's
+18.6%. This is disclosed and is not part of the claimed edge. On the
model-only period (2017-04-04 -> 2023-12-29) the strategy still makes
**49.68% CAGR / 44.51% max DD**, versus TQQQ **33.64% / 81.68%**. The pass is
not a warm-up artifact.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Session-shape features from 1-minute bars
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _session_features(symbol: str, end: str = END) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Daily session shape through the second-to-last 1-minute bar.

    The signal bar is `last - 1` (15:58 on a normal session); the entry bar is
    `last` (15:59). Highs, lows, close and volume use the signal bar, so the
    feature timestamp is strictly before the fill.
    """
    df = bt.load_1m(symbol)
    end_ts = pd.Timestamp(end, tz="America/New_York").normalize() + pd.Timedelta(days=1)
    df = df[
        (df["ts"] >= pd.Timestamp(START, tz="America/New_York"))
        & (df["ts"] < end_ts)
    ].reset_index(drop=True)
    dates = bt.session_dates(pd.DatetimeIndex(df["ts"]))
    first, last = bt.day_bounds_from_dates(dates)
    o, h, l, c, v = (df[k].to_numpy() for k in ("open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"))
    sig = last - 1
    i30 = np.minimum(first + 29, sig)
    j30 = np.maximum(sig - 29, first)
    hi = np.array([h[a:b + 1].max() for a, b in zip(first, sig)])
    lo = np.array([l[a:b + 1].min() for a, b in zip(first, sig)])
    vol = np.array([v[a:b + 1].sum() for a, b in zip(first, sig)])
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "date": pd.to_datetime(dates[first]),
        "open": o[first],
        "high": hi,
        "low": lo,
        "close": c[sig],
        "volume": vol,
        "c30": c[i30],
        "o30": o[j30],
        "entry": o[last],
        "n_bars": last - first + 1,
    })


def build_feature_panel(end: str = END) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """QQQ/TQQQ session features, 5-day means, and the 5-session label."""
    q = _session_features("QQQ", end)
    t = _session_features("TQQQ", end)
    m = q.merge(t, on="date", suffixes=("_q", "_t"))
    if not (len(m) == len(q) == len(t)):
        raise RuntimeError("QQQ/TQQQ session calendars do not align")

    oq, hq, lq, cq, vq = (m[k + "_q"].to_numpy() for k in ("open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"))
    ot, ht, lt, ct, vt = (m[k + "_t"].to_numpy() for k in ("open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"))
    c30q = m["c30_q"].to_numpy()
    o30q = m["o30_q"].to_numpy()
    entry = m["entry_t"].to_numpy(float)

    f = pd.DataFrame({"date": m["date"], "entry": entry})
    f["gap"] = oq / np.r_[np.nan, cq[:-1]] - 1.0
    f["first30"] = c30q / oq - 1.0
    f["mid"] = o30q / c30q - 1.0
    f["last30"] = cq / o30q - 1.0
    f["day"] = cq / oq - 1.0
    f["rng"] = (hq - lq) / cq
    f["clv"] = 2.0 * (cq - lq) / np.maximum(hq - lq, 1e-12) - 1.0
    vprev = pd.Series(vq).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean().to_numpy()
    f["volr"] = np.log(np.maximum(vq / np.maximum(vprev, 1.0), 1e-3))
    vtprev = pd.Series(vt).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean().to_numpy()
    f["tvolr"] = np.log(np.maximum(vt / np.maximum(vtprev, 1.0), 1e-3))

    # label: entry-to-entry return over the 5-session holding block
    f["y5"] = np.nan
    f.loc[: len(f) - 6, "y5"] = entry[5:] / entry[:-5] - 1.0

    # 5-day trailing means of the session-shape features
    names5 = {
        "gap": "gap5", "first30": "first30_5", "mid": "mid5",
        "last30": "last30_5", "day": "day5", "clv": "clv5",
        "volr": "volr5", "tvolr": "tvolr5", "rng": "rng5",
    }
    for col, name in names5.items():
        f[name] = pd.Series(f[col]).rolling(5, min_periods=4).mean().to_numpy()
    return f


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Walk-forward ridge on 5-session blocks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _ridge_fit(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, lam: float = LAM) -> np.ndarray:
    xb = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(x)), x])
    reg = np.full(x.shape[1] + 1, lam)
    reg[0] = 0.0
    return np.linalg.solve(xb.T @ xb + np.diag(reg), xb.T @ y)


def _standardize(xt: np.ndarray, xte: np.ndarray):
    med = np.nanmedian(xt, axis=0)
    xf = np.where(np.isfinite(xt), xt, med)
    mu = xf.mean(axis=0)
    sd = xf.std(axis=0)
    sd = np.where(sd > 1e-12, sd, 1.0)
    xs = np.clip((xf - mu) / sd, -5.0, 5.0)
    xes = np.clip((np.where(np.isfinite(xte), xte, med) - mu) / sd, -5.0, 5.0)
    return xs, xes


def walk_weekly(
    feat: pd.DataFrame,
    ts: pd.DatetimeIndex,
    features: list[str],
    *,
    refit: str = "MS",
    hurdle: float = 0.25,
    lam: float = LAM,
    min_train: int = MIN_TRAIN,
    purge_days: int = PURGE_DAYS,
    label: str = "y5",
    label_shuffle: int | None = None,
    feature_shuffle: int | None = None,
    feature_shift: int = 0,
    refit_end: str | None = None,
):
    """Expanding, purged walk-forward ridge on every 5th session.

    Returns the per-session prediction (only on block starts; NaN elsewhere),
    the training mean used for the hurdle, and the refit count.  Refits run
    from FIRST_REFIT to the last month in `ts` (or `refit_end`), so extending
    `ts` extends the walk-forward automatically (holdout-ready).
    """
    n = len(feat)
    blocks = np.arange(0, n, BLOCK)
    x = feat[features].to_numpy(float)
    if feature_shift:
        xs_all = np.full_like(x, np.nan)
        xs_all[feature_shift:] = x[:-feature_shift]
        x = xs_all
    lab = feat[label].to_numpy(float)
    pred = np.full(n, np.nan)
    base = np.full(n, np.nan)
    n_refit = 0

    if len(ts) == 0:
        return pred, base, 0
    end = (pd.Timestamp(refit_end, tz=ts.tz) if refit_end is not None
           else ts[-1].normalize())
    starts = pd.date_range(
        pd.Timestamp(FIRST_REFIT, tz=ts.tz), end, freq=refit
    )
    for qs in starts:
        qe = qs + (pd.DateOffset(months=1) if refit == "MS" else pd.DateOffset(months=3))
        test = (ts >= qs) & (ts < qe)
        if not test.any():
            continue
        tb = blocks[test[blocks]]
        if len(tb) == 0:
            continue
        tr = blocks[
            (ts[blocks] < qs - pd.Timedelta(days=purge_days))
            & np.isfinite(lab[blocks])
        ]
        if len(tr) < min_train:
            continue
        xt = x[tr].copy()
        yy = lab[tr].copy()
        if label_shuffle is not None:
            rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + label_shuffle * 97 + int(qs.value % 100000))
            yy = rng.permutation(yy)
        if feature_shuffle is not None:
            rng = np.random.default_rng(2000 + feature_shuffle * 89 + int(qs.value % 100000))
            xt = xt[rng.permutation(len(xt))]
        xs, xes = _standardize(xt, x[tb])
        ym, ys = yy.mean(), yy.std()
        if not np.isfinite(ys) or ys <= 0:
            continue
        w = _ridge_fit(xs, (yy - ym) / ys, lam)
        z = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(xes)), xes]) @ w
        pred[tb] = z * ys + ym
        base[tb] = ym
        n_refit += 1
    return pred, base, n_refit


def vol_target(feat: pd.DataFrame, c: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """45% volatility budget, using entry returns through session d-1."""
    px = feat["entry"].to_numpy(float) if "entry" in feat else np.asarray(c)[:, 1]
    lr = np.r_[np.nan, np.log(px[1:] / px[:-1])]
    sigma = pd.Series(lr).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std(ddof=0).to_numpy() * np.sqrt(252)
    sigma = pd.Series(sigma).shift(1).to_numpy()
    sigma = np.where(np.isfinite(sigma), sigma, np.nanmedian(sigma))
    return np.clip(VT / np.maximum(sigma, 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)


def expand_weekly(wb: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Hold each block-start weight for 5 sessions."""
    out = np.full(len(wb), np.nan)
    for b in range(0, len(wb), BLOCK):
        out[b:min(b + BLOCK, len(wb))] = wb[b]
    return out


def build_weights(
    ts: pd.DatetimeIndex,
    o: np.ndarray,
    c: np.ndarray,
    *,
    features: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    cell: dict | None = None,
    label_shuffle: int | None = None,
    feature_shuffle: int | None = None,
    feature_shift: int = 0,
    refit_end: str | None = None,
):
    """Causal daily target weights for the frozen model / a grid cell.

    `ts, o, c` are the daily panel (open/close per symbol).  The session-shape
    features are read from `features`, or rebuilt from 1-minute bars if not
    supplied.  Nothing after `ts[-1]` is used.  The walk-forward refits only on
    labels realised before each test month, with a 9-day purge.  `refit_end`
    is a reproducibility hook for the pre-freeze calendar; the default runs to
    the last month in `ts` (holdout-ready).
    """
    if cell is None:
        cell = GRID[0]
    if features is None:
        features = build_feature_panel()
    if len(features) != len(ts):
        raise ValueError("feature panel and daily panel lengths differ")
    fdates = pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.to_datetime(features["date"]).dt.tz_localize(ts.tz))
    if not np.array_equal(fdates, pd.DatetimeIndex(ts)):
        raise ValueError("feature panel and daily panel dates differ")

    pred, base, n_refit = walk_weekly(
        features, ts, cell["features"], refit=cell["refit"], hurdle=cell["hurdle"],
        label_shuffle=label_shuffle, feature_shuffle=feature_shuffle,
        feature_shift=feature_shift, refit_end=refit_end,
    )
    vt = vol_target(features, c)
    wb = np.where(
        np.isfinite(pred),
        vt * (pred >= cell["hurdle"] * base).astype(float),
        WARMUP_WEIGHT,
    )
    wb = np.clip(wb, 0.0, 1.0)
    w_daily = expand_weekly(wb)
    info = {
        "pred": pred,
        "base": base,
        "wb": wb,
        "vt": vt,
        "n_refit": n_refit,
    }
    return w_daily, info


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1-minute execution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def minute_weights(w_daily: np.ndarray, ts1: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> np.ndarray:
    """Expand a daily target to every minute bar.

    w_daily[d] is set at the 15:58 signal bar of session d and filled at the
    15:59 open, so from that signal bar through the next session's signal bar
    it is the active target.
    """
    dates_m = bt.session_dates(ts1)
    first, last = bt.day_bounds_from_dates(dates_m)
    sig = last - 1
    day_id = bt.day_ids(ts1)
    prev = np.r_[WARMUP_WEIGHT, w_daily[:-1]]
    w = np.where(np.arange(len(ts1)) >= sig[day_id], w_daily[day_id], prev[day_id])
    return np.clip(np.where(np.isfinite(w), w, WARMUP_WEIGHT), 0.0, 1.0)


def simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_daily, slip=1.0):
    wm = minute_weights(w_daily, ts1)
    ww = np.zeros((len(ts1), 3))
    ww[:, 1] = wm
    ww[:, 2] = 1.0 - wm
    r = bt.simulate(ts1, o1, c1, ww, band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    return r, bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def daily_series(values, ts):
    s = pd.Series(values, index=ts)
    d = s.groupby(s.index.date).last()
    d.index = pd.DatetimeIndex(d.index)
    return d


def yearly_table(ts1, equity, tqqq):
    eq = daily_series(equity, ts1)
    bq = daily_series(tqqq, ts1)
    out = {}
    for year in sorted(set(eq.index.year)):
        m = np.asarray([d.year == year for d in eq.index])
        if m.sum() < 2:
            continue
        out[str(int(year))] = {
            "strategy": float(eq[m].iloc[-1] / eq[m].iloc[0] - 1.0),
            "tqqq": float(bq[m].iloc[-1] / bq[m].iloc[0] - 1.0),
        }
    return out


def subperiod(ts1, equity, tqqq, start, end):
    eq = daily_series(equity, ts1)
    tq = daily_series(tqqq, ts1)
    m = np.asarray([(d >= pd.Timestamp(start)) and (d <= pd.Timestamp(end)) for d in eq.index])
    seg, bs = eq[m], tq[m]
    if len(seg) < 2:
        return None
    years = (seg.index[-1] - seg.index[0]).days / 365.25
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(seg)
    bpeak = np.maximum.accumulate(bs)
    return {
        "cagr": float((seg.iloc[-1] / seg.iloc[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1),
        "max_drawdown": float(-(seg / peak - 1).min()),
        "tqqq_cagr": float((bs.iloc[-1] / bs.iloc[0]) ** (1 / years) - 1),
        "tqqq_max_drawdown": float(-(bs / bpeak - 1).min()),
    }


def max_dd_window(ts1, equity):
    s = daily_series(equity, ts1)
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(s.to_numpy())
    dd = s.to_numpy() / peak - 1.0
    trough = int(np.argmin(dd))
    peak_i = int(np.argmax(s.to_numpy()[:trough + 1]))
    return {
        "peak": str(s.index[peak_i]),
        "trough": str(s.index[trough]),
        "drawdown": float(-dd[trough]),
    }


def quantile_stats(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
    return {
        "mean": float(np.mean(x)),
        "p5": float(np.percentile(x, 5)),
        "p50": float(np.percentile(x, 50)),
        "p95": float(np.percentile(x, 95)),
        "min": float(np.min(x)),
        "max": float(np.max(x)),
    }


def clean(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: clean(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [clean(v) for v in obj]
    if isinstance(obj, (np.floating, float)):
        v = float(obj)
        return v if np.isfinite(v) else None
    if isinstance(obj, (np.integer,)):
        return int(obj)
    if isinstance(obj, np.bool_):
        return bool(obj)
    return obj


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

    tsd, od, cd = bt.panel(("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"), START, END, "1D", warmup_days=0)
    ts1, o1, c1 = bt.panel(("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"), START, END, "1min", warmup_days=0)
    feat = build_feature_panel()
    if len(feat) != len(tsd):
        raise RuntimeError("feature panel / daily panel length mismatch")

    q, t, b = cd[:, 0], cd[:, 1], cd[:, 2]
    n = len(tsd)

    # --- grid -------------------------------------------------------------
    grid_rows = []
    preds = {}
    for cell in GRID:
        w_daily, info = build_weights(tsd, od, cd, features=feat, cell=cell)
        r, s = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_daily, 1.0)
        preds[cell["id"]] = (w_daily, info, r, s)
        first_pred = tsd[np.isfinite(info["pred"])][0] if np.isfinite(info["pred"]).any() else None
        grid_rows.append({
            "id": cell["id"],
            "features": cell["features"],
            "refit": cell["refit"],
            "hurdle": cell["hurdle"],
            "primary": bool(cell.get("primary", False)),
            "cagr": float(s["cagr"]),
            "max_drawdown": float(s["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(s["sharpe"]),
            "sortino": float(s["sortino"]),
            "volatility": float(s["volatility"]),
            "avg_tqqq_weight": float(np.mean(w_daily)),
            "fills": int(s["fills"]),
            "turnover": float(s["turnover"]),
            "first_prediction": str(first_pred.date()) if first_pred is not None else None,
            "pass_bar_1bp": bool(s["cagr"] > 0.3672 and s["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229),
        })

    primary_cell = next(c for c in GRID if c["id"] == PRIMARY)
    w_primary, info_primary, r_primary, s_primary = preds[PRIMARY]

    # --- cost ladder ------------------------------------------------------
    costs = {}
    primary_results = {}
    for slip in (1.0, 5.0, 10.0):
        r, s = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_primary, slip)
        primary_results[slip] = (r, s)
        costs[f"{int(slip)}bp"] = {
            "cagr": float(s["cagr"]),
            "total_return": float(s["total_return"]),
            "max_drawdown": float(s["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(s["sharpe"]),
            "sortino": float(s["sortino"]),
            "volatility": float(s["volatility"]),
            "exposure": float(s["exposure"]),
            "avg_tqqq_weight": float(np.mean(w_primary)),
            "fills": int(s["fills"]),
            "turnover": float(s["turnover"]),
            "ending_equity": float(s["ending_equity"]),
        }

    r1, s1 = primary_results[1.0]
    eq_daily = daily_series(r1["equity"], ts1)
    tq_daily = daily_series(c1[:, 1], ts1)
    qq_daily = daily_series(c1[:, 0], ts1)
    bil_daily = daily_series(c1[:, 2], ts1)

    # --- benchmarks -------------------------------------------------------
    benchmarks = {}
    for name, close in (("tqqq", c1[:, 1]), ("qqq", c1[:, 0]), ("bil", c1[:, 2])):
        bm = bt.benchmark(close, ts1, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        benchmarks[name] = {k: float(v) for k, v in bm.items()}

    # vol-target-only control
    vt_only = vol_target(feat, cd)
    r_vt, s_vt = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, vt_only, 1.0)
    benchmarks["vol_target_only_1bp"] = {
        "cagr": float(s_vt["cagr"]),
        "max_drawdown": float(s_vt["max_drawdown"]),
        "sharpe": float(s_vt["sharpe"]),
        "avg_tqqq_weight": float(np.mean(vt_only)),
        "fills": int(s_vt["fills"]),
    }

    # --- correlations -----------------------------------------------------
    strat_ret = eq_daily.pct_change().dropna()
    corr = {
        "strategy_vs_tqqq": float(strat_ret.corr(tq_daily.pct_change().dropna())),
        "strategy_vs_qqq": float(strat_ret.corr(qq_daily.pct_change().dropna())),
        "tqqq_vs_qqq": float(tq_daily.pct_change().corr(qq_daily.pct_change().dropna())),
    }

    # --- exposures / drawdown / yearly -----------------------------------
    exposure = {
        "avg_tqqq_weight": float(np.mean(w_primary)),
        "time_full": float(np.mean(w_primary > 0.98)),
        "time_zero": float(np.mean(w_primary < 0.02)),
        "switches": int(np.sum(np.abs(np.diff(w_primary)) > 0.02)),
        "first_prediction": str(tsd[np.isfinite(info_primary["pred"])][0].date()),
        "n_refits": int(info_primary["n_refit"]),
    }
    dd_window = max_dd_window(ts1, r1["equity"])
    yearly = yearly_table(ts1, r1["equity"], c1[:, 1])
    sub = {
        "2016-2019": subperiod(ts1, r1["equity"], c1[:, 1], "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
        "2020-2021": subperiod(ts1, r1["equity"], c1[:, 1], "2020-01-01", "2021-12-31"),
        "2022-2023": subperiod(ts1, r1["equity"], c1[:, 1], "2022-01-01", "2023-12-29"),
    }
    # model-only period (after the first prediction)
    first_pred_date = tsd[np.isfinite(info_primary["pred"])][0]
    model_period = subperiod(ts1, r1["equity"], c1[:, 1],
                             str(first_pred_date.date()), END)

    # --- simple-rule controls --------------------------------------------
    def rule_weights_weekly(sig, thr):
        wb = np.where(np.isfinite(sig), vt_only * (sig <= thr).astype(float), WARMUP_WEIGHT)
        return expand_weekly(wb)

    controls = {}
    clv5 = feat["clv5"].to_numpy(float)
    volr5 = feat["volr5"].to_numpy(float)
    volr = feat["volr"].to_numpy(float)
    control_weights = {
        "clv5<=0.25_weekly_xVT": rule_weights_weekly(clv5, 0.25),
        "clv5<=0.5_weekly_xVT": rule_weights_weekly(clv5, 0.5),
        "volr5<=0.25_weekly_xVT": rule_weights_weekly(volr5, 0.25),
        "volr<=0.25_daily_xVT": np.clip(np.where(np.isfinite(volr), (volr <= 0.25) * vt_only, WARMUP_WEIGHT), 0, 1),
        "vol_target_only": vt_only,
        "tqqq_buyhold": np.ones(n),
    }
    for name, w in control_weights.items():
        r_c, s_c = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w, 1.0)
        controls[name] = {
            "cagr": float(s_c["cagr"]),
            "max_drawdown": float(s_c["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(s_c["sharpe"]),
            "avg_tqqq_weight": float(np.mean(w)),
            "fills": int(s_c["fills"]),
        }

    # cost ladder for the two key simple-rule controls
    control_costs = {}
    for name in ("clv5<=0.25_weekly_xVT", "volr<=0.25_daily_xVT"):
        w = control_weights[name]
        row = {}
        for slip in (1.0, 5.0, 10.0):
            _, s_c = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w, slip)
            row[f"{int(slip)}bp"] = {
                "cagr": float(s_c["cagr"]),
                "max_drawdown": float(s_c["max_drawdown"]),
                "sharpe": float(s_c["sharpe"]),
            }
        control_costs[name] = row

    # provenance check: the pre-freeze calendar ended at 2023-10-01 and left
    # Nov-Dec 2023 on the 1.0 warm-up weight.  The primary above uses the full
    # calendar (holdout-ready).  Record the old-calendar number for the report.
    w_old, _ = build_weights(tsd, od, cd, features=feat, cell=primary_cell,
                             refit_end="2023-10-01")
    _, s_old = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_old, 1.0)
    frozen_calendar = {
        "refit_end": "2023-10-01",
        "cagr": float(s_old["cagr"]),
        "max_drawdown": float(s_old["max_drawdown"]),
        "sharpe": float(s_old["sharpe"]),
        "avg_tqqq_weight": float(np.mean(w_old)),
        "fills": int(s_old["fills"]),
        "note": "reproduces the pre-freeze scratch number exactly; Nov-Dec 2023 "
                "are held at the 1.0 warm-up weight because the old refit calendar "
                "stopped at 2023-10-01.  The primary headline uses the full calendar.",
    }

    # --- ablations (outside the grid) ------------------------------------
    ablations = {}
    ablation_sets = {
        "clv5_volr5": ["clv5", "volr5"],
        "clv5_only": ["clv5"],
        "volr5_only": ["volr5"],
        "last30_5_only": ["last30_5"],
        "gap5_first30_5_mid5": ["gap5", "first30_5", "mid5"],
        "full_shape": ["gap5", "first30_5", "mid5", "last30_5", "clv5", "volr5"],
    }
    for name, feats in ablation_sets.items():
        cell = {"id": name, "features": feats, "refit": "MS", "hurdle": 0.25}
        w_a, info_a = build_weights(tsd, od, cd, features=feat, cell=cell)
        r_a, s_a = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_a, 1.0)
        ablations[name] = {
            "features": feats,
            "cagr": float(s_a["cagr"]),
            "max_drawdown": float(s_a["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(s_a["sharpe"]),
            "avg_tqqq_weight": float(np.mean(w_a)),
            "fills": int(s_a["fills"]),
        }

    # --- placebo: shuffled labels and shuffled training features ----------
    n_placebo = 20
    placebo_label = []
    placebo_feat = []
    for seed in range(n_placebo):
        w_l, _ = build_weights(tsd, od, cd, features=feat, cell=primary_cell,
                               label_shuffle=seed)
        _, s_l = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_l, 1.0)
        placebo_label.append(float(s_l["cagr"]))

        w_f, _ = build_weights(tsd, od, cd, features=feat, cell=primary_cell,
                               feature_shuffle=seed)
        _, s_f = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_f, 1.0)
        placebo_feat.append(float(s_f["cagr"]))

    # timing placebo: features shifted by one block
    w_shift, _ = build_weights(tsd, od, cd, features=feat, cell=primary_cell,
                               feature_shift=BLOCK)
    _, s_shift = simulate_minute(ts1, o1, c1, w_shift, 1.0)

    placebo = {
        "shuffled_labels_20": quantile_stats(placebo_label),
        "shuffled_training_features_20": quantile_stats(placebo_feat),
        "shifted_features_5_sessions": {
            "cagr": float(s_shift["cagr"]),
            "max_drawdown": float(s_shift["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(s_shift["sharpe"]),
        },
        "real_cagr": float(costs["1bp"]["cagr"]),
        "label_percentile": float(np.mean(np.array(placebo_label) < costs["1bp"]["cagr"])),
        "feature_percentile": float(np.mean(np.array(placebo_feat) < costs["1bp"]["cagr"])),
        "note": "placebos use the same model, hurdle and cost; labels/features are "
                "permuted within each monthly training window, or the features are "
                "shifted one 5-session block for the timing test",
    }

    # --- cut tests --------------------------------------------------------
    def cut_test(cut_date):
        idx = int(tsd.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(cut_date, tz=tsd.tz), side="right"))
        idx = (idx // BLOCK) * BLOCK
        if idx <= 0 or idx >= n:
            return {"cut": cut_date, "skipped": True}
        ts_c, o_c, c_c = tsd[:idx], od[:idx], cd[:idx]
        feat_c = feat.iloc[:idx].reset_index(drop=True)
        w_c, _ = build_weights(ts_c, o_c, c_c, features=feat_c, cell=primary_cell)
        diff = np.abs(w_c - w_primary[:idx])
        return {
            "cut": cut_date,
            "cut_index": int(idx),
            "cut_session": str(tsd[idx - 1].date()),
            "n_compared": int(idx),
            "max_abs_weight_diff": float(np.max(diff)),
            "n_changed_gt_1e-12": int(np.sum(diff > 1e-12)),
        }

    cut_tests = [cut_test("2020-06-30"), cut_test("2022-06-30")]

    # --- pass / fail ------------------------------------------------------
    dev1 = costs["1bp"]
    pass_1 = bool(dev1["cagr"] > 0.3672 and dev1["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229)
    pass_5 = bool(costs["5bp"]["cagr"] > 0.3672 and costs["5bp"]["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229)
    pass_10 = bool(costs["10bp"]["cagr"] > 0.3672 and costs["10bp"]["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229)
    dd_target = bool(dev1["max_drawdown"] < 0.60)

    # --- result -----------------------------------------------------------
    out = {
        "agent": "family-ml-microstructure",
        "strategy": "Weekly close-location / participation ridge state model",
        "status": "passed" if (pass_1 and pass_5 and pass_10) else "negative_result",
        "hypothesis": (
            "5-day mean close location and volume participation predict the next "
            "5-session TQQQ return; a walk-forward ridge model holds TQQQ when the "
            "predicted return is above a fraction of the training mean, with a 45% "
            "volatility budget for risk control."
        ),
        "universe": ["QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"],
        "marks": "1m",
        "data": {
            "source": "local adjusted 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL bars, regular session",
            "start": START,
            "end": END,
            "holds_2024_2026": False,
            "feature_timestamp": "15:58 ET signal bar; fill at the 15:59 open",
        },
        "primary": PRIMARY,
        "parameters": {
            "features": ["clv5", "volr5"],
            "clv_definition": "2*(C-L)/(H-L)-1 through the 15:58 bar",
            "volr_definition": "log(V / trailing 20-session mean volume) through the 15:58 bar",
            "feature_average": "5-session trailing mean",
            "label": "entry(d+5)/entry(d)-1",
            "model": "ridge",
            "l2": LAM,
            "refit": "monthly (MS), expanding",
            "min_train_blocks": MIN_TRAIN,
            "purge_days": PURGE_DAYS,
            "blocks": "every 5 sessions",
            "hurdle": 0.25,
            "vol_target": VT,
            "warmup_weight": WARMUP_WEIGHT,
            "band": 0.02,
        },
        "windows": {"dev": costs},
        "pass": {
            "bar": {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229, "sharpe": 0.82},
            "at_1bp": pass_1,
            "at_5bp": pass_5,
            "at_10bp": pass_10,
            "dd_under_60": dd_target,
        },
        "benchmarks": benchmarks,
        "grid": grid_rows,
        "ablations": ablations,
        "exposure": exposure,
        "drawdown_window": dd_window,
        "correlation": corr,
        "yearly": yearly,
        "subperiods": sub,
        "model_period": model_period,
        "simple_rule_controls": controls,
        "simple_rule_control_costs": control_costs,
        "frozen_calendar_diagnostic": frozen_calendar,
        "placebo": placebo,
        "cut_tests": cut_tests,
        "family_purity": {
            "primary_features": ["clv5", "volr5"],
            "source": "intraday 1-minute session shape (close location and volume participation)",
            "excluded": [
                "daily realised volatility / drawdown / trend SMA / relative strength",
                "intraday range (rng) is excluded from the primary and the grid; an "
                "exploratory screen showed it acts as a volatility proxy",
            ],
            "vol_target_role": "risk control only, not a predictor",
        },
        "variants": {
            "pre_registered_grid": len(GRID),
            "primary_frozen": PRIMARY,
            "exploratory_screens_disclosed": (
                "next-open classifiers/regressions, shallow CART trees with/without rng, "
                "daily clv/volume gates, a 1-session-label weekly variant, and the "
                "weekly ridge feature/hurdle/refit surface"
            ),
        },
    }
    (OUT / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(clean(out), indent=2, allow_nan=False))

    # --- console ----------------------------------------------------------
    print(f"\n=== {PRIMARY} dev {START}..{END} (1-minute marks) ===")
    print(f"first prediction {exposure['first_prediction']}  refits {exposure['n_refits']}  "
          f"avg TQQQ weight {exposure['avg_tqqq_weight']*100:.1f}%")
    print(f"1bp : CAGR {dev1['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {dev1['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
          f"Sharpe {dev1['sharpe']:4.2f}  fills {dev1['fills']}  turnover {dev1['turnover']:.0f}x")
    print(f"5bp : CAGR {costs['5bp']['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {costs['5bp']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
          f"Sharpe {costs['5bp']['sharpe']:4.2f}")
    print(f"10bp: CAGR {costs['10bp']['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {costs['10bp']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
          f"Sharpe {costs['10bp']['sharpe']:4.2f}")
    print(f"TQQQ : CAGR {benchmarks['tqqq']['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {benchmarks['tqqq']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
          f"Sharpe {benchmarks['tqqq']['sharpe']:4.2f}")
    print(f"pass 1bp={pass_1} 5bp={pass_5} 10bp={pass_10}  dd<60={dd_target}")
    print(f"corr to TQQQ {corr['strategy_vs_tqqq']:.3f}  to QQQ {corr['strategy_vs_qqq']:.3f}")
    print(f"placebo label p95 {placebo['shuffled_labels_20']['p95']*100:.2f}%  "
          f"feature p95 {placebo['shuffled_training_features_20']['p95']*100:.2f}%  "
          f"real {dev1['cagr']*100:.2f}%")
    print("\ngrid:")
    for g in grid_rows:
        print(f"  {g['id']:28s} CAGR {g['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {g['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  "
              f"Sharpe {g['sharpe']:4.2f}  wt {g['avg_tqqq_weight']*100:5.1f}%  pass={g['pass_bar_1bp']}")
    print("\nyearly (strategy / TQQQ):")
    for yy, v in yearly.items():
        print(f"  {yy}: {v['strategy']*100:7.1f}% / {v['tqqq']*100:7.1f}%")
    print("\nsimple controls:")
    for k, v in controls.items():
        print(f"  {k:28s} CAGR {v['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {v['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sharpe {v['sharpe']:4.2f}")
    print("\ncut tests:")
    for c in cut_tests:
        print(f"  {c}")
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT / 'result.json'}")
